definitions.explanation: A large Australian marsupial that moves by hopping on its powerful hind legs and carries its young in a pouch.

examples.japanese: カンガルー⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{育|そだ}てる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧。
examples.english: Kangaroos raise their babies in their pouches.

examples.japanese: ⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧カンガルー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw kangaroos at the zoo.

examples.japanese: カンガルー⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{後|うし}ろ→後ろ：00683_ushiro⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{跳|は}ねる→跳ねる：04378_haneru⟧。
examples.english: Kangaroos hop on their hind legs.

notes:
カンガルー is a loanword from English "kangaroo," referring to the large hopping marsupial native to Australia.

KEY VOCABULARY:
- ⟦{有袋類|ゆうたいるい}→有袋類：23707_yuutairui⟧: marsupial (the animal category)
- ⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧: pouch
- ⟦{後|うし}ろ→後ろ：00683_ushiro⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧: hind legs
- ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧カンガルー: baby kangaroo (joey)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カンガルー⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{跳|は}ねる→跳ねる：04378_haneru⟧: a kangaroo hops
- カンガルー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧: kangaroo pouch
- カンガルー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧: to see a kangaroo

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kangaroos are strongly associated with Australia in Japanese culture. The kanji {袋鼠|ふくろねずみ} (literally "pouch mouse") exists but is virtually never used; katakana is standard.
